q1: SELECT DISTINCT INSTRUCTOR.ID, INSTRUCTOR.NAME, TEACHES.COURSE_ID FROM INSTRUCTOR LEFT OUTER JOIN TEACHES ON INSTRUCTOR.ID > TEACHES.ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT INSTRUCTOR.ID, INSTRUCTOR.NAME, TEACHES.COURSE_ID FROM INSTRUCTOR, TEACHES WHERE INSTRUCTOR.ID = TEACHES.ID

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 uses a LEFT OUTER JOIN with a condition that INSTRUCTOR.ID > TEACHES.ID, which means it only considers rows where the instructor ID is greater than the course ID. Q2, on the other hand, uses an INNER JOIN with the condition INSTRUCTOR.ID = TEACHES.ID, which means it only considers rows where the instructor ID is equal to the course ID.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when there is an instructor who teaches a course, but the instructor ID is not greater than the course ID.
